=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The PR DESCRIPTION's Verification section explicitly describes the helper being exercised under `bash -eu -o pipefail` against a stub that "succeeds on the third attempt for a command that fails twice, and fails with rc=1 after exactly five attempts for a command that always fails." The repo's standing convention (memory records repo_learnings and the existing retry-helper test pattern at `tests/test_workflow_gh_retry_fallback_contract.py:234-299`, which the Copilot review comment at PR review comment id 4061509965 points at) is that a new behavioral helper ships with an executable contract test that locks the retry / backoff / exhaustion semantics — not only a static text check.
  Expected change site: `tests/test_mark_stable_release_tag_refspec_contract.py` (new test alongside `test_workflows_retry_every_tag_push_with_a_bounded_backoff`) or a new test file modeled on the gh-retry fallback contract, extracting the `retry_push` body from one workflow, sourcing it under bash with a stub `git push` override, and asserting both the success-after-N-failures path (rc=0, two `::warning::` lines, observed sleeps in [2s, 6s]) and the exhaustion path (rc=1, five `::warning::` lines, one `::error::` line, elapsed time in [30s, 35s]).
  Evidence of absence: The added test `test_workflows_retry_every_tag_push_with_a_bounded_backoff` (lines 63-92 of `tests/test_mark_stable_release_tag_refspec_contract.py`) only asserts that the literal strings `"retry_push() {"`, `"for push_attempt in 1 2 3 4 5; do"`, and `"retry_push <push>"` appear in the workflow source, plus that the three bare push commands don't appear on their own line. It never extracts the helper, sources it under bash, or exercises it against any stub. The author performed the behavioral verification manually (per the PR DESCRIPTION's Verification section) but did not lock it in CI, so a future edit that breaks the retry, backoff, or exhaustion semantics would still pass CI — exactly the silent-breakage failure mode that run 35570966035 demonstrated. The Copilot inline review comment (PR review comment id 4061509965) and pass-1 reviewers google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, z-ai_glm-5_2, and qwen_qwen3.7-plus all flagged this same gap independently.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

- tests/test_mark_stable_release_tag_refspec_contract.py:test_workflows_retry_every_tag_push_with_a_bounded_backoff (lines 63-90) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The test asserts only that the workflow YAML contains the literal strings `retry_push() {`, `for push_attempt in 1 2 3 4 5; do`, and `retry_push <push>`. It never sources the helper, never stubs the wrapped command, and never asserts retry-on-failure, exponential backoff timing, or nonzero exit on exhaustion.
  WHY: A future edit that breaks the helper's actual behavior — for example changing `return 1` to `return 0` on the final failure, removing the `sleep`, or dropping the `::error::` emission — would pass this contract test and only surface at the next real release. The PR description itself notes the helper was verified manually under `bash -eu -o pipefail` ("succeeds on the third attempt for a command that fails twice, and fails with rc=1 after exactly five attempts"), but that verification was not encoded as a contract test. This repo's repo-learned patterns (memory records 0-3, 14, 26) consistently require executable contract tests for workflow/script changes, and the existing `test_workflow_gh_retry_fallback_contract.py` already demonstrates the pattern: extract the helper via regex, source it into a throwaway bash function with a stub command override, assert success-after-failure and exhaustion paths.

  PROBLEM: The new test only asserts that the literal strings `retry_push() {`, `for push_attempt in 1 2 3 4 5; do`, and `retry_push <push>` exist in the workflow YAML. It never extracts and executes the helper, so a broken `retry_push` — one that returns 0 instead of 1 on exhaustion, omits the `sleep`, or bails after a single attempt — would still pass CI.
  WHY: A future edit that breaks the helper's retry semantics (the exact failure mode run 35570966035 demonstrated) sails through this static-pattern assertion and only fails at the next real release run. The repo already has an executable retry-helper test convention at tests/test_workflow_gh_retry_fallback_contract.py:234-299 that mocks a command, counts invocations, captures sleep durations, and asserts both success-after-failure (rc=0, call count=2) and exhaustion (rc=1, call count=4, sleep log="30\n60\n120\n"). The PR description's own Verification section confirms the author manually ran the helper under `bash -eu -o pipefail` and observed both paths — that manual check was never automated.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The repo's established standard (confirmed by memory context and the existing test at tests/test_workflow_gh_retry_fallback_contract.py:234-299) requires that automation changes adding retry/backoff logic be paired with executable contract tests that lock the exact retry, backoff, and exhaustion behavior — not just static source-text checks. The Copilot review comment (id 4061509965) on line 78 explicitly requests this: "please add equivalent executable coverage for this workflow helper, ideally for both paths."
  Expected change site: tests/test_mark_stable_release_tag_refspec_contract.py (append alongside test_workflows_retry_every_tag_push_with_a_bounded_backoff) or a new test file.
  Evidence of absence: No diff hunk in tests/ extracts the `retry_push` body, sources it into a bash subprocess, mocks `git push` with a configurable exit code, or asserts rc/call-count/sleep behavior. The only test added is the static string-match test at lines 63-91. The PR description's Verification section describes a manual `bash -eu -o pipefail` run that was never codified as an automated test.
